CONTEXT, BEFORE CONCLUSIONS

Your source mix.

How the stories in your current view are distributed. Counts measure your feed selection, not the world's coverage or the accuracy of a claim.

Where are the bias ratings?

Political bias and factual reliability are unrated. Broadsheet has no licensed rating dataset and does not infer ratings from headlines, publisher location, or your reading habits. Source types describe the publisher, not a verdict on its reporting.

Topic tags come from source-feed topics, imported categories, and simple headline rules. They can miss or misclassify a story. Publisher base is not the location of an event. This edition does not yet match the same event across publishers.

Your own reading room.

Follow sources, filter by topics, and save combinations as channels. Drag the canvas to explore. Drag a card's dotted handle to move it, or its bottom corner to resize it. Focus either handle and use arrow keys for the same controls. Retained NASA stories can unfold in a card, so several complete articles can stay open together.

Scroll inside a card to read its excerpt. Use the canvas background to scroll around the workspace. Ctrl/Command + scroll zooms. H returns home. Layouts, channels, and saved stories persist in this browser.

News cards show bounded publisher feed excerpts and link to original articles. The retained NASA archive includes attributed prose and images. A feed refresh is available on the local Python server; the static edition is a saved snapshot with visible collection dates.

NASA does not endorse this independent reader. There are no invented articles or inferred political bias scores.
